M-T-002.mitigation: Use digital signatures for data integrity

M-T-004.mitigation: Implement input validation and data sanitization

M-T-005.mitigation: Use TLS 1.3 for data in transit

M-T-006.mitigation: Enforce cryptographic code signing — only firmware signed with a trusted key is accepted for execution

M-T-007.mitigation: Require cryptographically signed firmware updates — reject unsigned or unverifiable images

M-T-008.mitigation: Protect physical cable routing with cable duct, conduit, or armored cable to prevent tap and tampering

M-T-009.mitigation: Secure cable access points with tamper-evident seals or locked enclosures to prevent undetected splicing

M-T-010.mitigation: Restrict data flow to read-only access — disable write/command registers at protocol level

M-T-011.mitigation: Apply end-to-end integrity protection (HMAC or digital signature) on data flows crossing the safety boundary (EN 50742)

M-T-012.mitigation: Use only approved cryptographic algorithms and key lengths (NIST SP 800-131A, BSI TR-02102) — CR 4.3

M-T-FSAFE-001.mitigation: Define and implement a deterministic fail-safe output state for all process outputs (CR 3.6)

M-T-013.mitigation: Synchronize shared-memory and MMIO access between masters using locks, atomic operations, or memory barriers; re-validate data at the point of use to close TOCTOU windows

M-T-014.mitigation: Integrity-protect the acquisition path (signed or MAC-protected sensor frames) with replay protection (freshness/sequence); where cryptographic integrity is infeasible on legacy/analog field devices, compensate with segmentation and independent cross-checks

M-T-016.mitigation: Sensor fusion or redundancy cross-check to detect single-sensor manipulation

M-T-017.mitigation: Integrity-protect the command path (MAC/signature with replay protection); where cryptographic integrity is infeasible on legacy/analog field devices, compensate with zone/conduit segmentation and interlocks

M-T-018.mitigation: Command plausibility checks and interlocks against unsafe setpoints

M-T-019.mitigation: Enforce local safety limits independently of the command channel
